title: A-10 Player of the Year Robbie Avila trending toward TCU after return to Saint Louis blocked
content:
The best passing big man in college basketball could be headed to TCU. Robbie Avila, who was recently given a preliminary injunction to play a fifth season of college basketball, is trending toward joining TCU, according to a person briefed on the discussions who was not authorized to speak publicly.

Avila had yet to sign as of Thursday morning, and the details of when he’ll be able to play were still being sorted. Nov. 11 was the first day of scheduled graduate enrollment appointments for the winter session and spring 2027 at TCU. If Avila can enroll (or has already enrolled) in a graduate program now, he may be eligible right away. Dec. 21 is the first day of classes for the four-week mini session at TCU, which would be the next window to enroll and begin classes.

Avila intended to return to Saint Louis, and St. Louis City Circuit Court Judge Jason Sengheiser ruled that the 15-player roster cap could be lifted to make room for him. But the College Sports Commission denied Saint Louis’ request to add a 16th player, announcing Friday that the school couldn’t do so because it had opted into the House settlement.

Saint Louis coach Josh Schertz had planned to have Avila suit up last Friday against Missouri, but the school was notified of the CSC’s decision hours before the game and decided not to have Avila in uniform.

Instead of fighting the CSC’s ruling, Avila started looking for a new spot to play. TCU is a solid landing spot. The Horned Frogs returned four of their top seven from last year’s team that reached the Round of 32 of the NCAA Tournament. TCU was left with a hole in its frontcourt after leading scorer David Punch transferred to Texas.

Avila, the Atlantic 10 Player of the Year last season, is a much different player than Punch, but he’s an upgrade over what the Horned Frogs had already. He’ll likely eventually start next to Xavier Edmonds, giving TCU potentially one of the best frontcourts in the Big 12.

TCU is 3-0 but won its latest game over Louisiana-Monroe in double overtime. Sophomore DJ Thomas, who averaged 6.6 points per game last year at West Virginia, is starting next to Edmonds. TCU is also without Texas Tech transfer center Luke Bamgboye, who has missed the last two games with a lower-body injury and is set to miss the next five weeks, according to 247Sports. If Avila signs with TCU, once he is cleared and back in game shape, he’ll likely take that spot. It’ll be the first time in his college career that he does not play for Schertz, whom he followed from Indiana State to Saint Louis.
